- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.  
- After a spike in price (forecast > true outcome by >5%), reduce subsequent forecast by 2–3% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and forecast deviates >3% from true, apply a smoothing filter to reduce volatility bias.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 period lag in price correction.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.6 → -0.4 → +0.2), reduce forecast volatility and favor smoother, trend-following adjustments.
